assumptions.choice: Opposite entry signal only closes the existing position (flat); it does not immediately open a new position in the opposite direction on the same bar
assumptions.reason: Spec's '(reverse/close)' phrase is ambiguous; treated as terminology clarification rather than an instruction to pyramid into a new position, consistent with the canonical one-position-at-a-time default. A fresh entry can occur on a later bar once flat, following the normal entry rules.

assumptions.choice: stop_distance computed from ATR[0] evaluated at the bar the entry order actually fills (not the earlier signal bar)
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'stop_distance = ATR[0] * atr_mult ... at entry'; since entry executes on the bar after the signal, ATR[0] at that fill bar is the literal 'ATR at entry'.

assumptions.choice: Implemented the ATR stop as a native backtrader Stop order (exectype=bt.Order.Stop) submitted immediately after entry fill, rather than a manual close-price comparison each bar
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'when the ATR stop triggers', implying an order-level trigger; a broker-managed stop order is the closest literal, idiomatic backtrader mechanism for this and is checked/triggered automatically each bar.
